candidates.change_summary: Remove the onlyOwner modifier from withdrawAll so anyone can call it, changing the balance after a call.
Delete the withdraw call inside withdrawAll so it does nothing, leaving the contract balance unchanged.
Change the onlyOwner modifier requirement to always revert, making withdrawAll always fail.
Remove the require check in onlyOwner so anyone passes the modifier, allowing non-owner to drain.
Replace the transfer call with a no-op, keeping only the require(false) revert, ensuring withdraw always reverts.
Replace the recipient of the transfer from msg.sender to the zero address, causing funds to be burned instead of sent to the owner.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier check entirely, allowing anyone to call withdraw and change the balance.
Replace the low-level call with a regular transfer to make the sendMoney function revert if transfer fails, changing sendMoney's behavior so it no longer returns success result to caller.

Remove the require statement that checks the call result, so sendMoney silently fails to transfer Ether but still returns successfully, changing the observable behavior regarding whether Ether was actually sent.
Delete the entire body of sendMoney, making it a no-op that does not transfer any Ether, so the balance of the contract and the recipient remain unchanged after the call.
Use msg.sender as the target of the low-level call instead of the _target parameter, altering which address receives the Ether and thus changing the observable effect of sendMoney.
Replace require with an inverted require that passes only when the call fails, making sendMoney succeed only when no Ether is actually sent, fundamentally changing its semantics.
Remove the require check from the onlyOwner modifier, allowing any caller to invoke functions guarded by it, including sendMoney, thus changing the access control observable behavior.
